chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he was asked
about the killing of the quail and the stone, is it permissible to eat from it? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.الْبُنْدُقِ: Quail or a specific type of bird/meat
key_terms.الْحَجَرِ: Stone (often referring to a specific type of bird or meat in this context)

ai.seo_question: Is the meat of the quail and stone (al-bunduq wa al-hajar) halal to eat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of consuming the quail (*al-bunduq*) and the 'stone' (*al-hajar*), likely referring to a specific type of bird or a term of art in classical fiqh. The concise 'no' response indicates a prohibition, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise classification of game animals (*sayd*) and their slaughter methods. This ruling is foundational for understanding the nuances of *dhik* (mentioning God's name) during the hunting of specific avian species.
